html:
The Nyikina are an Aboriginal Australian people of the lower Fitzroy River in the west Kimberley of Western Australia, near Derby. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. They call the river Mardoowarra, and it lies at the centre of their law and stories.

Their neighbours were the Warwa and Nimanburu to the northwest, the Unggumi to the north and the Mangala to the south. Sheep and cattle stations took over the Fitzroy plains from the 1880s, and Derby was founded as their port in 1883. Many Nyikina worked on the stations, and in recent years they have campaigned against damming the river.
